=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel — buyer-side review

## Executive assessment

The Seller’s update is **not a balanced package for Wattlebridge**. It would leave the Buyer paying AUD 24 million for the shares while potentially inheriting facility debt, transaction bonuses, unresolved IP ownership and an unquantified data incident. At the same time, the proposed disclosure, knowledge and liability provisions could make recovery difficult.

The immediate priorities are to:

1. Make **Riverlark repayment and security release simultaneous with Completion**, and ensure the funds flow delivers a genuinely debt-free/cash-free transaction.
2. Require **effective Bluefen consent, with its conditions satisfied**, before Completion.
3. Obtain payment evidence and an effective **Ironquay IP assignment**, backed by a broader specific indemnity.
4. Investigate the export incident and negotiate a **specific indemnity and appropriate pre-Completion protections**.
5. Reject the blanket application of general warranty limits, broad disclosures and buyer-knowledge exclusions to all claims.

The Seller’s “reviewer efficiency note” and “[STANDARD]” labels do not establish that Wattlebridge accepted those positions. They require the same scrutiny as the rest of the Seller’s draft.

## Material issues and pushback

### 1. Riverlark: debt and security must be cleared at Completion

DD-003 records approximately **AUD 3.2 million outstanding**, with no repayment or final security discharge yet evidenced. A release after Completion is inconsistent with the debt-free/cash-free baseline: the Buyer could acquire a company still owing the debt and subject to security, without control over the release process.

**Push for:**

- A binding payout and release letter from Riverlark stating the amount due at Completion and the steps for unconditional release of all relevant security.
- **Simultaneous repayment from the Seller’s proceeds at Completion**, with releases delivered then or under an agreed bank release undertaking and prompt registration/perfection steps.
- A funds flow and price adjustment that do not make Wattlebridge pay the AUD 24 million price **and** bear the same debt. Review the treatment of cash, debt-like items and any agreed working-capital mechanism as a whole.
- Confirmation of the change-control requirements in DD-003 and whether any consent or waiver is also needed.

### 2. Bluefen: consent must be effective, not merely delivered

Bluefen represents approximately **AUD 3.6 million of FY26 revenue, or 30%**. DD-002 identifies a change-control consent clause and associated conditions; the disclosure letter says no final written consent or evidence satisfying those conditions has been provided. “Reasonable endeavours” and automatic satisfaction upon delivery of a consent could leave the Buyer with a consent that is conditional, ineffective or commercially adverse.

**Push for:** an express condition precedent requiring a valid, unconditional written consent—or one on terms acceptable to the Buyer—and satisfaction or waiver of all applicable conditions before Completion. Require the Seller to obtain it, keep the Buyer informed, and avoid accepting changes to commercial terms without Buyer approval. Include a long-stop date and termination rights if it is not obtained. Review the actual consent against clauses 11.2–11.3 before clearing the condition.

### 3. Seller-favourable limitations and remedies

The proposed general cap is **AUD 4.8 million**, with an AUD 25,000 de minimis, an AUD 250,000 tipping-*excess* basket, and an 18-month notice period. Those terms materially restrict recovery even for substantiated losses. More importantly, the Seller proposes to extend limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions to **all claims**, while putting title and capacity under the same general regime.

**Push for:**

- A separate **fundamental warranty regime** covering at least title, ownership, authority and capacity, with a cap up to the purchase price, longer notice periods, and no general de minimis or basket.
- Separate, appropriately longer periods and caps for **tax**, and negotiated protection for IP.
- Express carve-outs from general limitations for **specific indemnities, purchase-price adjustments, Completion obligations and equitable relief**, as applicable. Preserve claims for fraud and other liabilities that cannot lawfully be excluded; do not allow non-reliance language to undermine them.
- A materially improved general regime: a higher cap and longer notice period, a lower de minimis, and a **first-dollar basket** once the threshold is exceeded. At minimum, ensure qualifying claims aggregate consistently and no overlapping drafting prevents recovery.
- Clear notice, claim-continuation and mitigation provisions so a claim notified in time is not lost through an impractical procedural requirement.

These are negotiation positions; the final cap and periods should reflect diligence, insurance availability and the commercial bargain. Review clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 together rather than fixing one while another overrides it.

### 4. Disclosure and Buyer knowledge could extinguish otherwise valuable protection

Schedule 7 and paragraphs 1.1–1.2 purport to disclose the entire data room, accounts, registers and public records. Clause 8.3 goes further, excluding matters the Buyer or advisers knew or could have discovered. Together these could transfer broad, unidentified risks to Wattlebridge, including risks not apparent from a document without investigation.

**Push for:** disclosure only of matters **fairly disclosed with sufficient detail** to identify the nature and scope of the issue against the relevant warranty, in a specifically identified disclosure letter and documents actually made available in a defined, frozen data room. Reject deemed disclosure of public records and anything merely discoverable. Delete the broad Buyer-knowledge exclusion; if a compromise is unavoidable, confine it to actual knowledge of specifically named individuals, without imputed adviser knowledge or a duty to investigate. Neither disclosure nor knowledge should qualify negotiated specific indemnities unless expressly agreed.

The specific disclosures still warrant attention: they identify issues but often leave key facts unresolved. Paragraph 1.4’s reservation does not itself resolve whether action, payment or notification is required.

### 5. Ironquay: ownership of project materials is not established

DD-004 makes transfer of SOW3 Project Materials conditional on **cleared payment of every SOW3 fee**. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open, but is not independent proof of non-payment; equally, the data room contains neither a receipt nor a confirmatory assignment. The current indemnity covers only the specific payment, not the wider consequences of a defective transfer.

**Push for:** independent evidence that all SOW3 fees have cleared and an effective confirmatory assignment from Ironquay covering the relevant materials and rights, with any necessary further assurances. Broaden the specific indemnity to cover losses, claims and remediation arising from unpaid amounts, failure of transfer or competing rights—not just the AUD 180,000 payment. It should not be defeated by general disclosure, knowledge, thresholds or the general warranty cap.

### 6. Export/privacy incident: investigate before allocating an unknown exposure

DD-006 records a link sent to an unintended external address, potentially involving approximately **1,240 records**. Access, precise scope and any notification requirement remain unknown. This is **not established to be a confirmed breach**, but neither is there a basis to dismiss it as immaterial.

**Push for:** prompt preservation of evidence, access and download-log review, confirmation of recipients and data scope, containment, and legal assessment of any notification or remediation obligations. Obtain updates and access to findings before Completion. Negotiate a specific indemnity for losses and reasonable investigation, response and remediation costs arising from the incident, with an agreed control and cooperation procedure and protection from the general limitations. Consider a Completion condition or other protection if diligence shows a material unresolved exposure.

### 7. Completion bonuses: seller cost must not silently become Buyer debt

DD-005 records **AUD 420,000** of bonuses conditional on Completion and continued employment, omitted from the funds flow. Their actual accrual, eligibility and associated payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs have not been established. If the Company pays them after Completion without an adjustment, the Buyer bears a transaction-related cost despite the Seller’s statement that it is the Seller’s matter.

**Push for:** an employee-by-employee schedule, legal and payroll treatment, and explicit allocation of the bonuses and applicable on-costs to the Seller. Reflect the agreed amount in the Completion funds flow or debt/debt-like adjustment, with a true-up for conditional amounts, and avoid double counting. Confirm who pays employees and when.

### 8. Supplier renewals: do not assume ordinary-course or debt-like treatment

The three Sandbar renewals total **AUD 330,000**. DD-008 and DD-011 must be read together, and the disclosure does not establish whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.

**Push for:** the contracts, renewal dates, notice and termination rights, invoices and accounting treatment. Allocate any pre-Completion accrued liability or Seller-triggered transaction cost through the agreed price mechanism where appropriate; do **not** automatically treat all future ordinary-course expenditure as debt. Restrict non-ordinary renewals between signing and Completion without Buyer consent.

### 9. Tax and IP need their own coverage

Applying the general warranty regime to tax and IP leaves potentially significant exposures subject to an 18-month period, general cap and broad disclosure. In particular, the Ironquay issue illustrates why an open-ended assertion that IP is settled is insufficient.

**Push for:** a tax covenant/indemnity for pre-Completion tax liabilities, with appropriate periods, claim procedures and interaction with price adjustments; robust tax warranties; and IP warranties addressing ownership, licences, infringement claims and rights needed to operate the business. Coordinate these with the specific Ironquay protection and avoid double recovery.

### 10. Title verification and other contract points

- **Share title:** DD-012 records Harbourglass as holder of 100% of issued shares, but does not prove every aspect of good, unencumbered title. Verify the register against corporate records, share issuances and transfers, and check for encumbrances and rights affecting the shares. Require title and authority warranties, transfer instruments, board approvals and delivery of the relevant registers at Completion.
- **Office lease:** DD-007 identifies a notification obligation, not a stated consent requirement. Confirm timing and responsibility and procure the required notice; do not assume landlord consent is required without reviewing the lease.
- **Mossvale:** DD-009 restricts assignment but does not state that a share sale itself requires consent. Check the whole agreement and transaction structure before requesting a consent; address any actual notice, change-control or assignment requirement.

## Recommended negotiating sequence

1. **Before signing:** obtain the underlying DD documents, full SPA and funds flow; verify title and quantify the debt, bonuses and renewal positions. Begin Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay and incident work immediately.
2. **In the markup:** reject blanket disclosure, discoverability and all-claims limitations; establish separate fundamental, tax and specific-indemnity regimes.
3. **As Completion protections:** require effective Bluefen consent, simultaneous Riverlark payoff and release, and satisfactory Ironquay payment/assignment evidence. Resolve incident protection in light of the investigation.
4. **Before agreeing the funds flow:** reconcile the AUD 24 million price with debt-free/cash-free mechanics, bonus allocation, on-costs and any justified adjustments, ensuring no item is counted twice.

This assessment is based on the Seller’s summary and disclosure letter, not the complete SPA or underlying DD records. Those documents must be reviewed before finalising drafting or clearing conditions.
